From: Brian Fields, CLEVELAND

Dear Sir,

I am writing to you after having
written for some information
regarding the Rotronic Wafadrive
Unit to Mr. Jim Hossack. He
passed on your name and address
saying if anyone would be able
to help on this matter you
would.

I've been given a new Wafadrive
unit which I had hoped to
replace my cassette loading
situation on my ZX 48K computer
but I have not been able to find
anyone who could supply me with
the wafa drive cassettes to
match this wafadrive unit.

I wonder if you know or have any
idea of how I could get hold of
these type of tapes?

Any help at all in this matter
wuld be greatly appreciated
indeed.

        Yours faithfully,

          Brian Fields

Brian Cavers to Brian Fields

From: Terry Filby, SUFFOLK

Dear Brian,

Last year there was a letter in
OUTLET complaining about the
service, or lack of it, by
Daniel Garner. I believe that
particular problem was resolved,
and I hope my own experience
will be too.

I joined the +3 Users Group some
time ago (No. 427), got several
things from them; PD Software,
etc., which was all received
promptly. It was a good service.

Then, the new mag. started and
out of the first issue I ordered
3 Sam disks for six pounds.

I sent a cheque for the amount
on 16-5-1991, and it was cashed
by Mr Garner on 24-5-1991.
Despite several letters and
phone calls, including my last
letter in which I asked for
either the disks or a refund, I
have, to date, received neither.

        Yours Sincerely,

           Terry Filby

Brian Cavers to Terry Filby




I rang Daniel Garner who assured
me that his records showed he
had despatched the discs but he
also told me he had been plagued
by a lot of packets going astray
in the mail. His local sorting
office seems particularly bad in
this respect. He promised me he
would immediately send you a new
set of discs and you should have
received these by now.

                         Brian

From: Bill Coats, STRATHCLYDE

Dear Brian/Ron,

In the letters section on Disc
No.53 I was asking for a
solution to my problem of having
to BREAK back to BASIC and RUN
my programs again before the
printer would operate (I have a
+3 Spectrum [23354/23355 bug]
and a Citizen 120D+ printer).

I had phoned PCG about this some
time ago when I found that when
using their DTP program I was
having to BREAK and RUN (the two
POKES had been put in, as well
as FORMAT LPRINT "U"). I was
told it was "just one of those
things".

On loading Disc No.54, if I then
select "6" (FONTWIST.3) from the
menu it loads and operates
normally (by the way, you hadn't
messed it up!). TABLOID also
prints first time. Now, I made a
copy of "FONTWIST.3" and added
the two POKES, and guess what? I
still need to BREAK and RUN. I
even tried the following loader
program: "10 POKE 23354,62: POKE
23355,16: LOAD "FONTWIST.3"
thinking that if the POKES were
inserted before the program was
loaded this would cure the
problem, alas no.

I've found that if the POKES are
inserted from the keyboard first
then the program LOADed, the
printer works first time - but

this is just the same as BREAK
and RUN. It's as if the POKEs
aren't effective until a program
is RUN - or something.

So there must be something in
the CONTENTS program which irons
out that problem.

So, come on, all you wizards out
there, don't leave it all to
Brian. I'm sure he has enough on
his plate!!

Oh for a Spectrum without a bug
... I suppose it's better then a
virus!

                    Bill Coats

Brian Cavers to Bill Coats

I think the answer is in the
"DISK" loader program in OUTLET.
At lines 1001 and 1002 are two
machine code routines in REM
statements.These are called with
GO SUB 1001 and GO SUB 1002. I
think the one at 1002 is the +3
printer bug POKEs you're already
using (or rather, their machine
code equivalent) and the one at
1001 is one that fixes that
annoying "return to loader menu
on error" syndrome.It seems most
likely that 1001 sets certain
flags and solves your problem.
This may be a red herring but it
seems the most promising reason
as to why "FONTWIST.3" works in
OUTLET but not separately.

To extract it you will need to
delete everything else and just
leave 1001. The CHEZRON header
lines are invisible but they are
just lines 1 to 8.

Before saving, it would be best
to renumber it to say, 9000 (and
put a GO SUB 9000 at say,line 10
in FONTWIST) because 1001 is
right in the middle of the
FONTWIST BASIC but do not "edit"
1002 itself to renumber it or it
may corrupt. If you don't have a
renumber program then put a line
in front of it in FONTWIST to
jump over it using GO TO 1002.

Whatever line number used, MERGE
it into FONTWIST.3 and put a GO
SUB to it at say, line 10. Let
me know if it works!     - Brian

Brian Jones, 17 Strawberry Close
Birchwood, Warrington. WA3 7NT.


Firstly may I compliment you on
a very good magazine.

I have a DTP called Enigma which
is meant for the 48k. Is it
possible to convert to run on +3
as it only saves and loads from
tape not disc? [Files corrupt
screen on loading from disc]. If
not are there any DTP's for the
+3, and if so,where from and how
much?

Does M3Unlock allow you to save
M3 progs to drive B: and then
run them without using M3 to
re-load them?

Are there any P.D.Libraries for
the +3 for progs such as DTP,
Art, Music etc?

Could you send me a catalogue of
your own PD?

Can anyone tell me where I can
get a copy of CPM +3 Version?

As I have not got a printer of
my own yet I hope it is okay to
send in my letters on disc using
Tasword2 filename OUTLET?

             Thanks,

          Brian Jones

To Brian Jones from Brian Gaff

What a lot of questions! Anyway,
here goes.

The PCG DTP suite is still the
only one I know of that works on
the +3. It consists of three
programs that link together if
you have all three: WORDMASTER,
the word processor (`13.95),
HEADLINER, the graphic and title
designer (`10.95) and TYPELINER,
the desktop publisher (`18.95).
The whole "DTP PACK"of the three
programs is available for `37.95
but add `2 if wanted on +3 disc
(also available on tape or +D).
Write to P.C.G.,61 School Street
Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria,LA14
1EW

We did have a review but it was
way back in Issue 8 - before the
+3 version was available but you
can always get the tape version!
Send P.C.G an SAE for details or
phone 0229 836957. Always tell
suppliers you heard of them in
OUTLET as it does help us and
therefore YOU!

PD libraries seem to be mainly
stocked with Outlet Freeware, so
I doubt if you will find much
joy there but try PROPAC (see
OUTBOARD).

The Enigma tapes had some nice
programs on it, but I do not
recall the DTP system. I have no
idea why drive loads would
corrupt screens. The fact that
it runs from disc would mean the


commands are in Basic, so that
should work no matter what you
loaded from. I do know that a
lot of 48K programs used the old
printer buffer as a convenient
place to store things, so maybe
the program corrupts system
variables. [I do have the Enigma
DTP and transferred it to +3
with no problem.Try it again and
check every change carefully as
you may have got something wrong
(say, a code length) - B.C.]

M3 Unlock can allow loading from
the B: drive in some cases. You
would need to alter the loader a
bit. Some would not work due to
the use of CODE as part of the
loader. Remember that any
unlocked program that corrupts
the screen, leaves it that way.

If you contact me directly [see
address in OUTBOARD under B.G.],
I will be talking to Locomotive
Software to see if they still
produce CP/M for the +3. If they
do, I think the price is around
`29. You may be able to buy it
cheaper second hand, of course,
but make sure it's complete, has
no disc errors and the manual is
still there!
                           B.G.

Bit more from Brian Cavers...

Regarding sending letters on +3
disk - YES! We PREFER a textfile
as it saves us time and expense
typing it all in again. We don't
have a separate P.D. list but I
have sent you our back issues
list.                      B.C.

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Brian and Ron,

The problem Mr. Les Tyler is
having with the printer going
missing when using 80T drive
could well be connected with the
SYSTEM boot file.

I have a small advantage in that
I have had correspondence with
Les in the past and have more
info on his set up. Unless he
has changed things he is using a
Disciple but using the RS232
port on the 128 to a serial
printer.

All he has done is to change the
drive from 40T to 80T.

I would guess the problem he
encountered could be the SYSTEM
VARIABLE 11 (select printer) is
set wrongly on some of the 80T
discs in the BOOT file.

As this POKE@ 11 has a quirk and
tends to be once-set-then-forget
it may be of interest to others.
It does crop up at odd times in
programmes but not too often.

The POKE@ 11 tells the Disciple
or +D if the Centronics parallel
port (set to "0" )is to be used
or the Spectrum printer port
(set to "1").

This is usually set in the DOS
when first customised, the
SYSTEM file then simply copied
from disc to disc.

Now for the quirk. If the system
is booted with it set to "1"
(use Spectrum port) then
POKE @ 11,0 will change to the
Disciple printer output. It can
be either a direct POKE or it
can be written into the program.

However, if booted to use the
Disciple port then doing a POKE@
11,0 will NOT change the printer
over to use the Spectrum.

It is not necessary to start
from scratch with the initial
set up tape. Simply enter POKE@
11,1 then resave the SYSTEM file
in the normal way. On next boot-
ing with this new DOS the
Spectrum port will be used
automatically.

It is worth mentioning that
UNIDOS does things a bit differ-
ently. Why, I do not know - but
it's reversed! "1" to use
Disciple,"0" to use Spectrum. It
does have the advantage that I
believe it will change in both
directions by doing a POKE @ 11
with "1" or "0".

Also every time POKE @ 11,1 is
used, it automatically sends the
printer initialisation codes
(the set that are sent auto-
matically on boot).

Again, a point to watch,it sends
the codes if set to "1" but once
sent then the value is changed
(to 129 ) to tell the DOS not to
send them again.

If the DOS is resaved once codes
have been sent then the value
129 will in the SYS file. On
boot, printer codes will NOT be
sent. Therefore, before resaving
DOS file turn off printer and do
a POKE @ 11,1 to ensure the disc
copy holds "1". This does not
apply obviously if using the
Spectrum printer port.

There seems to be an error on
the SET UP program for UNIDOS.
However, this may have been
corrected in later versions.

Line 625 change the POKE@ 90,128
to POKE@ 89,128

Line 638 change LET disp=90 to
LET disp=89

COPYRIGHT: I wrote a program
based loosely on an idea from a
TV quiz show which I sent to
Chezron for their scrutiny. An
issue or so later there was a
comment about items and games
that could resemble other copy-
right games and the chances of
being sued. That set me think-
ing. Where did my game stand
being based on a TV show that
was itself copyright of a TV
company?

The easy way out would be to
tell Chezron not to use the
program so I wrote to the TV
company, briefy described my
"game" and asked if it came
within their copyright and would
they give approval for it to be
included in a disc magazine.

I had a very quick reply (I
actually had 3 quick replies.
Don't let me hear any moans
about not getting replies from
companies!) I leave room here
for Brian to add "look whose
talking".

The first was to tell me that my
letter had been passed to their
business section connected with
the programme.

The second from the commercial
side confirmed they held the
copyright to all aspects of the
program and anything derived
from the program. Nothing could
be used without the due licens-
ing agreements and royalties.
They had passed my letter to the
section that dealt with this.

OH HECK! Thinks I. What have I
got into? This is getting out of
hand! I only wrote a few K of
BASIC loosely based on just one
aspect of the program!

I was on the point of writing to
tell them to forget it but
decided to wait.

I am glad I did because I had a
third letter from a very nice
man. A very, very nice man who,
without going into the whole
detail, said that my program did
not appear to conflict with
their copyright and providing it
was not named after or connected
with their program there would
not be any problem.

The point of this is to indicate
that it could be only too easy
to fall foul of copyright, i.e.
related to the program name for
example, but a simple enquiry to
interested parties produced a
satisfactory outcome all round.

I would think Brian and Ron
would agree with me in saying if
anything is sent in that is not
100% original by sender then to
mention such as where the idea
originated, or perhaps program-
ming containing sub routine that
came from other sources to
mention this.

Note previous comment in OUTLET
about discs under heading of PD
but are in fact copyright.

I nearly fell into the trap of
sending a program to OUTLET that
contained a subroutine that I
included for my own personal
benefit but was not my own
original. When I checked I found
it was from a magazine and was
marked (C).

          Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

Thanks, Malcolm. Yes, I'm not
surprised that the TV companies
have extensive and sophisticated
machinery for dealing with copy-
right licensing because this is
a HUGE market for them. Because
your program only uses the maths
PRINCIPLE (which in fact is an
old, well-established puzzle,
long before COUNTDOWN used it)
and because you don't use the
title "COUNTDOWN" or anything
similar or make it look related
in any way (by say, putting a
digitized picture of Carol
Vorderman on the title page)then
they don't mind (in fact in my
view I don't believe they CAN do
anything).              - Brian

From: Les Tyler, CHELTENHAM

In connection with your detailed
reply to my query regarding
printing difficulties with
COL80+ and the RS232 on the 128K
Sinclair,this is of only limited
interest to most readers, I
reckon, seeing as how they all
seem to have parallel printers!
Therefore, I decided to restrict
my feedback to a Tasword 128
letter, which will be really for
your information and perhaps
guidance to others who might
come up with similar problems in
the future.

First of all, very many thanks
for coming back so quickly on
the question, I had only posted

it mid-to-late January so didn't
expect to see any comeback until
the March Issue at the earliest!
Your speedy reply enabled me to
get some useful suggestions be-
fore I had even run the February
Issue of OUTLET, you can't get
faster sevice than that!

I had a letter from Malcolm
Perry, (who had supplied me with
the 80-track drive in the first
place), which eventually pointed
me on the right track, and I'm
pleased to say I seem to have
solved the problem perfectly as
a result of his advice and in
fact have also cleared another
related problem that I wrote
about some months ago with
regard to a print-out of OUTDEX,
again via the RS232 port.

I am, in addition, hoping I will
also have cleared yet another
snag, this time with UNIDOS,
which might well be a product of
the same bug. I hope so, anyway.

It looks as if I owe you some
sort of apology...my interface
is a DISCIPLE, not a +D!!
Perhaps I should have made this
clear in the first place, but
presumed that you might well be
aware of that fact, so left any
mention of the I/F out of my
query file. So, much of your
reply was, unfortunately based
on a wrong premise, and I do
apologise for involving you in
so much time and effort on my
behalf; it is certainly highly
appreciated, you may be sure.

Like you, I could not understand
why, using the larger capacity
drive but with no other alter-
tions to soft or hardware, I
could get no response from the
printer, it just did not seem
possible, which is why I raised
the query of whether or not the
MGT drive had some sort of link
inside it to be made or un-made
as appropriate. Malcolm assured
me this was not so but suggested
that one possible area of con-
fusion could be the SYSTEMS file
on the disc. As I'd set these up
myself, (the 5.25 drive one way
back when INDUG first published
their updated to the DISCIPLE
versions 3c and 3d), and as both
worked normally in practically
all cases except with COL80+ I

was not very confident this
would be the source of trouble.

However, sleeping on it, I woke
suddenly during the night with a
shriek of "E U R E K A !!" Like
the young gentleman who went to
bed with a problem on his mind
and woke up to find... (I'll say
no more, the ladies might be
listening!),the old brain cells
had finally grasped what Malcolm
was trying to say,and I got down
there and then, (5 a.m!) to
check it out.

It transpired that the trouble
was indeed with the Systems
file, I had set up the 5.25
version correctly, taking the
"no printer" option as I did not.

have a parallel printer, but had
not done the same with the 3.5
discs, as Malcolm had supplied a
few formatted discs with the
drive and I had been using his
version, which worked perfectly
well except when it came to
printing, his being for parallel
printer usage!

I rummaged around in my box of
bits and pieces and eventually
unearthed the original DISCIPLE
setting-up tape,ran it,formatted
a new disc, transferred COL80+
and one of the OUTLET text files
and...IT WORKED! I then tried to
print out OUTDEX via the RS232.
Usually I had had to install
Interface 1,go into 48K mode and
print in that mode when I wanted

copies of OUTDEX and that worked
as well! A most happy gent
settled down to breakfast, I can
assure you!

One small problem raised itself
later, when I found that now I
could not print out TASWORD 128
files, which I had been doing
happily enough before! But this
was, of course, 'easy-peazy'
now, as I knew that the system
code was now version 3b, and
needed to be upgraded again to
3d. Luckily, I still have all
copies of FORMAT, so was able to
extract the relevant upgrading
programs of 5 years ago and do
the necessary. This letter is
being printed with the new set-
up, so clearly everything is
working correctly again.

The foregoing pearls of wisdom,
(or whatever you care to call
them!)all point to one important
fact...NEVER rely on old, (OR
other people's!) system files,
they are highly likely to be
different from your own, espec-
ially when it comes to the per-
ipheral uses, they may work for
many things but will come un-
stuck eventually!

Best not to cut corners but
completely reinitialize the
systems file if changing the
drive and/or interface!

A final point concerning your
reply, where you mention the
fact that COL80+ does not have a
serial facility.

Quite right, but it does have
the User Option,which I'd adapt-
ed to suit my needs. Basically,
it entailed removing much of the
parallel printer-related program
lines and substituting RS232
ones as necessary, in particular
a new line:
   9896, "LET L$="":FORMAT
   "P";baudrate.
I have always found COL80+ to be
extremely useful and efficient,
and could not have used it
without the serial option, I
rate it as one of the most
useful utilities published in
OUTLET. I did have a go at the
original COL80 version, but
found it far too slow, so was
highly delighted when the later
version came along and I was
able to convert it as required.

I note you are hopeful of the
Spectrum continuing into the
next century, if so it will
probably outlive me, rapidly
approaching the "threescore
years and ten" mark. May I wish
both of you all the best for
this year and the future, let us
hope you don't buckle under the
strain of coping with all these
queries we keep firing at you!!

          All the best

            Les Tyler

Brian Cavers to Les Tyler

I don't agree that your reply is
not worth publishing as I'm sure
other readers use the RS232
output and all these ideas need
to be aired and exchanged.In any
case, the principle of using the
wrong DOS and getting problems
applies to other areas.

Your other comment about alter-
ing COL80+ emphasises what I've
said over and over in OUTLET: to
help me solve your problems I
need ALL the information you can
give me. That reminds me, yes,it
is best to repeat your system
details, like Disciple etc. as I
deal with so many people I can't
always remember who has what!

Reject completely the "THREE-
SCORE-YEARS-AND-TEN" theory!It's
based on misleading statistics
taking into account chances of
disease, accident and so on but
has nothing to do with the real
ageing of the body or with YOU
as an individual.

See you next century!
                       - Brian

From: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON

This is just a note on the sub-
ject of sending disks and other
magnetic material through the
post.I have sent disks and tapes
through the post many times, as
well as having received them.
Sometimes, the disks can get
corrupted in the post,as someone
mentioned in a recent letter.

I know this because I have test-
ed disks before sending them and
they can still arrive corrupted
at the other end.

However, I have had no problems
(so far) with cassettes. I think
this has something to do with
the way the information is
stored.

For example, normal IBM 5.25"
360k disks were the only disks
to survive when I recently had a
parcel of disks sent to me. The
1.2Mb 5.25" disks were all
corrupted in some way.

All the cassettes I have sent
and received in the post have
been OK as well. This could be
because the information is
stored in narrow tracks on 3.5"
and high density 5.25" disks.


The 360k 5.25" disk uses a wider
recording strip, as does a
normal cassette tape. So what
can you do to protect your data?
ALWAYS make sure you have a
backup copy before posting.

Sending data on cassette rather
than disk sounds a good idea,
but it usually inconveniences
both parties.

Don't rely on a label on your
letter such as"MAGNETIC MEDIA"or
somesuch. These markings(includ-
ing "FRAGILE") can't be seen
when the item is upside-down or
at the bottom of a postbag.

There is no substitute for care-
ful packaging: You can prevent
some of the stray magnetic
fields reaching your disks by
lining your Outlet wallet with
kitchen foil. If you send disks
on their own, try just wrapping
the disk, or make your own card-
board wallet.

For the physicists among you,
this creates a Faraday Cage, so
magnetic energy travels around
the outside of the tinfoil
rather than straight through the
disk. That's the theory anyway!

You can get special disk-mailers
but these are usually just a
cardboard wallet lined with some
kind of material which does the
same job as the tinfoil.

These ideas only cost a few
pence so why not give them a
try? They are not 100 percent
guaranteed but they may well
stop some of your disks being
corrupted.
            Mike Pike
                        more...

PS.The Post Office's recommend-
ation (in their leaflet "Wrap Up
Well") is to use a box with at
least 4 inches of soft packing
all around!
               Mike Pike


To Mike Pike from Brian Gaff

Well, we send many discs through
the post and very few are
returned as faulty. The most
common problem is drives that
are slightly out of alignment.

A magazine did some tests on
corruption a few years ago. The
only postal corruption they had
was traced to the disc being
close to a motor in a train. The
A/C field can be quite strong,
as you can imagine.

By the way, as an aside, never
put a floppy on top of a CD
player, as many have large
permanent magnets in the disc
clamp!               - B.G..

From: Brian Fields, CLEVELAND

Dear Sir,

Dear Brian and Ron,

The problem Mr. Les Tyler is having with the printer going missing when using 80T drive could well be connected with the SYSTEM boot file.

I have a small advantage in that I have had correspondence with Les in the past and have more info on his set up. Unless he has changed things he is using a Disciple but using the RS232 port on the 128 to a serial printer.

All he has done is to change the drive from 40T to 80T.

I would guess the problem he encountered could be the SYSTEM VARIABLE 11 (select printer) is set wrongly on some of the 80T discs in the BOOT file.

As this POKE@ 11 has a quirk and tends to be once-set-then-forget it may be of interest to others. It does crop up at odd times in programmes but not too often.

The POKE@ 11 tells the Disciple or +D if the Centronics parallel port (set to "0" )is to be used or the Spectrum printer port (set to "1").

This is usually set in the DOS when first customised, the SYSTEM file then simply copied from disc to disc.

Now for the quirk. If the system is booted with it set to "1" (use Spectrum port) then POKE @ 11,0 will change to the Disciple printer output. It can be either a direct POKE or it can be written into the program.

However, if booted to use the Disciple port then doing a POKE@ 11,0 will NOT change the printer over to use the Spectrum.

It is not necessary to start from scratch with the initial set up tape. Simply enter POKE@ 11,1 then resave the SYSTEM file in the normal way. On next boot- ing with this new DOS the Spectrum port will be used automatically.

It is worth mentioning that UNIDOS does things a bit differ- ently. Why, I do not know - but it's reversed! "1" to use Disciple,"0" to use Spectrum. It does have the advantage that I believe it will change in both directions by doing a POKE @ 11 with "1" or "0".

Also every time POKE @ 11,1 is used, it automatically sends the printer initialisation codes (the set that are sent auto- matically on boot).

Again, a point to watch,it sends the codes if set to "1" but once sent then the value is changed (to 129 ) to tell the DOS not to send them again.

If the DOS is resaved once codes have been sent then the value 129 will in the SYS file. On boot, printer codes will NOT be sent. Therefore, before resaving DOS file turn off printer and do a POKE @ 11,1 to ensure the disc copy holds "1". This does not apply obviously if using the Spectrum printer port.

This is just a note on the sub- ject of sending disks and other magnetic material through the post.I have sent disks and tapes through the post many times, as well as having received them. Sometimes, the disks can get corrupted in the post,as someone mentioned in a recent letter.

I know this because I have test- ed disks before sending them and they can still arrive corrupted at the other end.

However, I have had no problems (so far) with cassettes. I think this has something to do with the way the information is stored.

For example, normal IBM 5.25" 360k disks were the only disks to survive when I recently had a parcel of disks sent to me. The 1.2Mb 5.25" disks were all corrupted in some way.

All the cassettes I have sent and received in the post have been OK as well. This could be because the information is stored in narrow tracks on 3.5" and high density 5.25" disks.

The 360k 5.25" disk uses a wider recording strip, as does a normal cassette tape. So what can you do to protect your data? ALWAYS make sure you have a backup copy before posting.

Sending data on cassette rather than disk sounds a good idea, but it usually inconveniences both parties.

Don't rely on a label on your letter such as"MAGNETIC MEDIA"or somesuch. These markings(includ- ing "FRAGILE") can't be seen when the item is upside-down or at the bottom of a postbag.

There is no substitute for care- ful packaging: You can prevent some of the stray magnetic fields reaching your disks by lining your Outlet wallet with kitchen foil. If you send disks on their own, try just wrapping the disk, or make your own card- board wallet.

For the physicists among you, this creates a Faraday Cage, so magnetic energy travels around the outside of the tinfoil rather than straight through the disk. That's the theory anyway!

You can get special disk-mailers but these are usually just a cardboard wallet lined with some kind of material which does the same job as the tinfoil.

These ideas only cost a few pence so why not give them a try? They are not 100 percent guaranteed but they may well stop some of your disks being corrupted. Mike Pike

Проблема мистера Les Tyler с исчезновением принтера при использовании 80-дорожечного дисковода вполне может быть связана с загрузочным файлом SYSTEM.

У меня есть небольшое преимущество: я раньше переписывался с Les и знаю больше деталей о его конфигурации. Если он ничего не менял, то он использует Disciple, но подключен через порт RS232 на 128 к последовательному принтеру.

Единственное, что он сделал, — это заменил дисковод с 40 на 80 дорожек.

Я предполагаю, что возникшая проблема вызвана тем, что СИСТЕМНАЯ ПЕРЕМЕННАЯ 11 (выбор принтера) на некоторых 80-дорожечных дисках в файле BOOT установлена неверно.

Поскольку у этого POKE@ 11 есть одна странность, и его обычно выставляют по принципу «настроил и забыл», это может быть интересно и другим. Время от времени это всплывает в программах, хотя и не слишком часто.

POKE@ 11 указывает Disciple или +D, какой порт использовать: параллельный Centronics (значение "0") или порт принтера Spectrum (значение "1").

Обычно это настраивается в DOS при первоначальной конфигурации, а затем файл SYSTEM просто копируется с диска на диск.

А теперь о странности. Если система загружена с настройкой "1" (использовать порт Spectrum), то команда `POKE @ 11,0` переключит вывод на принтер Disciple. Это может быть как прямой ввод POKE, так и команда внутри программы.

Однако если при загрузке был выбран порт Disciple, то выполнение `POKE @ 11,0` НЕ переключит принтер обратно на Spectrum.

Вовсе не обязательно начинать все с нуля с установочной кассеты. Просто введите `POKE @ 11,1`, а затем пересохраните файл SYSTEM обычным способом. При следующей загрузке с этой обновленной DOS порт Spectrum будет выбираться автоматически.

Стоит отметить, что в UNIDOS все устроено несколько иначе. Почему — не знаю, но там все наоборот! "1" — использовать Disciple, "0" — использовать Spectrum. Зато у нее есть преимущество: насколько я помню, она переключает вывод в обоих направлениях с помощью `POKE @ 11` со значениями "1" или "0".

Кроме того, каждый раз при вызове `POKE @ 11,1` она автоматически отправляет коды инициализации принтера (тот набор, который отправляется автоматически при загрузке).

Опять же, важный момент: она отправляет коды, если установлено значение "1", но как только они отправлены, значение меняется (на 129), сообщая DOS, что повторно отправлять их не нужно.

Если DOS пересохранить после отправки кодов, то значение 129 останется в файле SYS. При загрузке коды принтера отправлены НЕ БУДУТ. Поэтому перед повторным сохранением файла DOS выключите принтер и выполните `POKE @ 11,1`, чтобы копия на диске содержала "1". Естественно, это не относится к случаям, когда используется порт принтера Spectrum.

Кажется, в программе SET UP для UNIDOS есть ошибка. Впрочем, в более поздних версиях ее могли исправить.

### От: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON

Это просто заметка на тему отправки дисков и других магнитных материалов по почте. Я много раз отправлял диски и кассеты по почте, а также получал их. Иногда диски могут портиться при пересылке, как кто-то упоминал в недавнем письме.

Я знаю это, потому что тестировал диски перед отправкой, и они все равно могли прийти поврежденными.

Однако у меня (пока что) не было проблем с кассетами. Думаю, это как-то связано со способом хранения информации.

Например, обычные диски IBM 5.25" 360k были единственными, которые выжили, когда мне недавно прислали посылку с дисками. Диски 1.2Mb 5.25" были повреждены в той или иной степени.

Все кассеты, которые я отправлял и получал по почте, также были в порядке. Это может быть связано с тем, что информация записывается на узкие дорожки на 3.5-дюймовых и высокоплотных 5.25-дюймовых дисках.

360k 5.25-дюймовый диск использует более широкую дорожку записи, как и обычная кассета. Так что же можно сделать, чтобы защитить свои данные? ВСЕГДА делайте резервную копию перед отправкой.

Отправка данных на кассете, а не на диске, кажется хорошей идеей, но обычно это доставляет неудобства обеим сторонам.

Не полагайтесь на надписи на письме вроде «MAGNETIC MEDIA» или тому подобные. Эти отметки (включая «FRAGILE») не видны, когда посылка лежит вверх ногами или на самом дне почтового мешка.

Ничто не заменит бережной упаковки: вы можете предотвратить воздействие некоторых блуждающих магнитных полей на ваши диски, выстелив конверт Outlet обычной кухонной фольгой. Если вы отправляете диски отдельно, попробуйте просто обернуть диск или сделать собственный картонный конверт.

Для физиков среди вас: это создает клетку Фарадея, так что магнитная энергия проходит по внешней стороне фольги, а не прямиком сквозь диск. По крайней мере, такова теория!

Можно достать и специальные почтовые конверты для дисков (disk-mailers), но обычно это просто картонный конверт, проложенный каким-то материалом, выполняющим ту же работу, что и фольга.

Эти идеи стоят всего пару пенсов, так почему бы не попробовать? Они не дают стопроцентной гарантии, но вполне могут уберечь некоторые из ваших дисков от повреждения данных.
            Mike Pike
